audit_items.proof_trace: Replay prevention relies on a physical DELETE (L83) instead of an `is_used` flag, but the implementation uses two separate RPC calls — `get_authorization_code` (L70) and `delete_authorization_code` (L83) — with no atomicity guarantee. A concurrent second request can call `get_authorization_code` and retrieve the same auth code before the first request's DELETE executes, causing both requests to hold a valid `authCode` in memory and pass all downstream validation (client_id, redirect_uri, expiry at L101-106, PKCE). The developer comment at L82 acknowledges TOCTOU risk but the chosen mitigation (non-atomic separate RPC calls) does not eliminate the race window.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A malicious OAuth client sends two parallel POST requests to /oauth/token with an identical valid auth code and code_verifier before either request's `delete_authorization_code` RPC completes; both requests pass all validation and receive independent 30-day access tokens from a single auth code exchange.
